summary: MILESTONE 2 (Following ecosystem) tested end-to-end on BOTH web and mobile against the shared backend. All 10 backend pytest cases pass (who-to-follow interleaved + actor_type filter + reasons for demo & freeuser; dismiss not_interested/hide persists; follow imported 50k-catalog station imp_fun_talk_1003_uae -> appears under /social/following stations with station_kind='imported' and unfollow removes it; follow/status accurate; non-existent station 404; M1 regression — moments create + feed-v2 following shows is_mine; wall like/save/share persist). Web Home renders [data-testid=who-to-follow] with 10 interleaved cards, Follow (person) -> API 200 and card is removed (verified by card count 10->9), Not Interested & Hide also remove the card instantly, and composer publish fires [data-testid=fuusic-confetti] (success toast 'Your post has been shared!' shown). FollowingPanel at /social/following shows all 6 categories (People, Creators, Advisors, Businesses, Stations, Clubs). Mobile Expo /social/following renders [testID=following-screen] + [testID=who-to-follow] with 10 cards, follow/notinterested/hide all remove the card, and Moments tab moment-composer -> moment-post triggers [testID=confetti-burst]. No critical or minor issues found.

critical_code_review_comments: WhoToFollow.jsx follow() removes the card after 900ms post-success — fine, but if a user double-taps during the busy state it is correctly gated by `disabled`. No action needed.
social_discovery.py uses a hard-cap of 40 in the route (good) and services/who_to_follow.py excludes self/blocked/followed/dismissed at the DB layer (good).
